svg.title: Regions, sites and sectors
svg.desc: A small global plane holds people, roles, sign-in, module classes, designs, policies, the address plan, roll-ups and the audit archive, and copies what regions need to each regional plane. Each region (Europe, Americas, Asia-Pacific) has its own regional plane that manages its sites; each site is one data centre with several sectors, each sector one Incus cluster. Sites in a region are linked by OVN interconnection and backup copies; regions are linked by published services and archives only.
svg.text: people, roles and sign-in · module classes · designs and versions
policies · address plan · roll-ups · audit archive
copies of people, roles, classes, designs and policies (regions keep working without it)
the regional plane manages its sectors over ~30 ms; the management link of ADR 0008
OVN interconnection over the regional backbone; backup copies (tier 2) stay in the region
published services with mutual TLS; archives (tier 3) only where policy allows; no shared networks
Fabric → region → site → sector (one Incus cluster, up to 50 servers) → server. 10 regions × 5 sites × 20 sectors × 50 servers = 50,000 servers (estimate).
